entities.name: Taper damage morphology
observations: Retrieval research uses visual scores, maximum-depth measurements, and FIB cross-sections to assess head–stem taper damage; a matched 120-pair study found no significant score difference for microgrooved versus smooth tapers (head P=.14; stem P=.35). PMID:28111124.
Morphology is informative but visual grading alone is imperfect and cannot reliably separate fretting from corrosion contributions.

entities.name: Coupled taper material loss
observations: An adaptive finite-element study modeled more than four million gait cycles and mechanical plus chemical removal, comparing predicted loss patterns with retrieved taper damage; cyclic micromotion/fretting and electrochemical corrosion are plausible interacting processes. PMID:36354540.
Damage patterns can test mechanistic hypotheses when combined with metrology and modeling, but do not alone prove causal mechanism.

entities.name: Taper loss quantification
observations: Retrieval studies quantified loss volume in a subset of 48 recalled dual-taper implants and compared fretting/corrosion and volumetric loss for metal versus ceramic heads on one CoCr stem design; available summaries did not report effect sizes. PMID:30277996; PMID:28566326.
